note: Small National Park Service campground at the Jacks Fork / Current River confluence at the end of Highway V east of Eminence, inside Ozark National Scenic Riverways. The drive-in loop is set back from the river behind the park road, a lawn and the walk-in tent sites on the bank. Gravel spurs are short: one site is posted for a 28-ft RV and the rest for 20 ft or less, so a 23-ft rig has a single site to book. No dump station. Cell service is unreliable. --Claude
summary: Confirmed year-round, reservation-only on recreation.gov, 22 sites, $20 peak / $10 off-peak, no hookups; facilities and seasonal fees written. FIT QUESTION: only site 003 (28 ft) is posted long enough for a 23-ft rig. PIN MOVE ~790 m (stored pin is the rec.gov facility point across the river). Not waterfront stands. Phone 573-323-4236.
flags: OWNER QUESTION / POSSIBLE DROP (rig length): per-site RV/Trailer limits on recreation.gov are 15 ft on sites 001, 002, 005 and 010, 18 ft on 004, 20 ft on 006 and 007, and 28 ft on 003; sites 008, 009, 011 and 012 list no RV or trailer at all (tent, vehicle or pickup camper), 013-019 are walk-in tent sites and the cluster sites are tent-only ('Six tents maximum per site on the Cluster Sites. No RV's.'). NPS says 'RV: Sites 1-12 (limited size)'. So exactly one site, 003, is posted for a 23-ft motorhome, and 006/007 at 20 ft are under even the 21-ft 'tight' line. Kept with the caveat in the note because one site does fit; under the ~20-ft rule this is close to a drop - owner's call. Stored '~13 RV-capable' was wrong (8 by the records).

SITE 020: the record lets RV and Trailer to 30 ft, but its Max Vehicle Length attribute is 0, it has no notice, its coordinate (37.19021,-91.27469) is at the edge of the gravel bar 130 m east of the loop, and NPS describes '3 sites located near the gravel bar' as backcountry sites at $10. Read as a data error, not a second RV site; max_rig_ft written 28.

PIN MOVE: stored 37.1939,-91.2828 is the recreation.gov facility point, in forest on the far (north-west) side of the Current River about 790 m from the campground. Proposed 37.18931,-91.27600 (centre of the drive-in loop, sites 001-012; NPS's own point is 37.189929,-91.276297, at the day-use lot by the river).

WATERFRONT - NOT WATERFRONT STANDS: the drive-in loop is 60-120 m south of the river (site 006 nearest, about 70 m) with the park road, a mown lawn, the walk-in tent row and the timbered bank between. Sites 013-019 (walk-in tents) sit at the top of the bank 20-30 m from the water. recreation.gov tags every one of the 22 sites 'Riverfront', including the cluster sites and the back of the loop - a facility-wide tag, not evidence. No upgrade lead for RV sites.

FEES BY TYPE: standard $20 (Apr 15 - Oct 15) and $10 (Oct 16 - Apr 14); tent-only $10 all year; cluster sites $45 peak / $25 off-peak. The NPS reservation text and the calendar agree that winter nights are reservable (no first-come season now; the old 'First-come, First-served Season' rows in the rate table end in April 2025).

WINTER WATER: NPS lists potable water as 'Yes - seasonal' and the flush restroom as closed in winter (it gives 'October 30 - April 14' in one place, recreation.gov 'April 15 to Oct.15'); a vault toilet by the boat launch is year-round. Treat winter as dry camping.
PHONE (lead, not written by apply): no phone stored; NPS and recreation.gov give (573) 323-4236 (campground operations, weekdays 8:00-4:30); recreation.gov's contact line also gives (573) 561-0580.
ACCESS: 'Paved Roads - All vehicles OK' (NPS); Highway V ends at the campground. Site spurs are gravel. NPS: 'Not accessible by wheelchair', no camp host, camp store seasonal.
